ownerContracts: New scalar owner covers exactly30 PCR words and LP_UART/LP_GPIO. Other UART/I2C/Transport/SARADC/SHA/BootClock/APM owners remain responsible for their real engines. SDK named-field POR is an explicit virtual profile; known TRM1.1 disagreements remain in the source receipt.

Only named clock closes, idempotent current writes, PAU held-reset assertion and zero-only CLK_OUT/LP_GPIO are accepted. Reserved/source/divider/RO mutations, reset release or enabling unimplemented engines reject transactionally.

Strict selected ROM eagerly creates the peripheral owner. RMT MMIO/ticks/IRQ/completed-frame draining/scheduler deadlines all honor actual stored gate bits. Unsupported strict RMT MMIO becomes Fault::Unsupported/ModelLimit with guest exception CSRs unchanged. The unselected SRAM path keeps existing RMT behavior.

First selection refuses an active/IRQ/pending-frame legacy RMT controller before creating profile state. CPU retains; HP restores PCR; LP restores LP_UART/LP_GPIO; raw deselection drops the owner even with pending reset.

TG1 APB/reset low bits publish to actual TimgWdt inputs after the previous watchdog/reset boundary. TG0/TG1 ordinary timer clocks are independent from MWDT functional sources; APB closure blocks registers without stopping the separately clocked watchdog.
Six APM register clock modes select automatic0/always-on1, preserve actual constrained Machine qualification and all filter/TEE/CPU/DMA decisions, and have distinct HP/LP declared reset groups.
LP clock-to-pad zero does not change internal LP_FAST/SLOW/PLL/CPU/watchdog/timer clocks. The real LP_IO close loop observes both LPPERI27 and LP_GPIO0; RNG24 closure prevents later samples.
Core/HP reset preserves the complete LPPERI owner: LP_IO/RNG clock, reset/config, deterministic sample count and sequence. Only declared LP/Chip reset restores its POR.
Strict LPPERI reads/writes settle the old watchdog timeline and reject pending/overdue-reset access before changing gates or requesting another sample. Unselected legacy behavior remains unchanged.

controls.legacyApmRangeCount: 18 to21 because three newly supported exact clock words fall within the old enumerated interval; other old assertions retained

actualNative.description: Unchanged firmware executes the full peripheral shutdown and later UART reconfiguration, then stops at the next unimplemented cache-error interrupt setup word. Native exitCode0 is a completed diagnostic probe, not product acceptance.

negativeResults.boundary: Before this change, original read6009603c at42000e20 stopped after26601352steps/26601344cycles/UART2194.

limits: No app_main, LCD, buttons, TF or radio execution acceptance. Clock configuration is not a physical readiness/calibration claim.
Focused LTO=false checks do not replace final default-LTO full-workspace CI, CPU controls, production WASM/browser validation or fresh acceptance.
Raw captures and personal paths are excluded; commands use named pinned inputs. Aggregate elapsed times and measured counts are retained.

priorValidation.scope: Initial eight-case integration; passed405 tests and both Clippy, but did not cover complete LPPERI HP retention or pending-reset boundaries. Independent review found two P2 defects despite passing checks.

reviewRepairs.before: HP reset reconstructed LPPERI while preserving LP_GPIO, reopening LP_IO/RNG and reseeding the virtual sample source.
reviewRepairs.after: Non-LP reset transfers the complete prior LP owner. A real-MMIO control compares both latches and RNG count/sequence against an unreset controller; LP reset restores POR.

reviewRepairs.before: Strict LPPERI read/write bypassed the old-watchdog/pending-reset barrier.
reviewRepairs.after: Both access directions settle and check the reset boundary before invoking the owner. Actual MMIO cases cover manual pending and overdue130M MWDT and preserve unselected behavior.
